newsitem.title: UK: Tengiz-Novorossiisk pipeline tariff set at $25/ton.
newsitem.headline: Tengiz-Novorossiisk pipeline tariff set at $25/ton.

text.p: The pipeline tariff for Kazakh Tengiz crude on the planned link to the Black Sea terminal Novorossiisk has been set at $25 per tonne, Ed Smith, general director of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's (CPC) said on Friday.
Smith told an industry conference that the rate of increase in the tariff would be in line with the U.S. producer price index, and that a price cap of $38 had also been set.
"The tariff price will be capped at $38 or at the level when all the investment has been repaid," he said.
Tariffs for crude oil joining the pipeline at Kropotkin were currently calculated at $7.75 per tonne.
"Of course if there are times where there is spare capacity and there are shippers looking to move material the tariffs would be negotiable," said Smith.
The first Kazakh crude oil will start flowing through pipeline by late 1999, he said. The construction of the 1,500 kilometre pipeline has been under negotiation since 1992.
"The first oil should start flowing through the pipeline on a commercial basis as of November 1 1999," said Smith, who is also a project executive at the Oman Oil Company, a CPC shareholder.

He said that final details of a deal signed by the consortium, comprising Russia, Kazakhstan and Oman as well as nine international oil companies, in December 1996 would be finalised in the very near future.
"It's just a question of dotting the I's and crossing the T's," he said.

He said that under the final deal, the existing consortium would be separated into two legal bodies to be known as the Caspian Pipeline Consortium Russia (CPCR) and Caspian Pipeline Consortium Kazakhstan (CPCK) which would be managed by a common management structure.
He said the management team would be headed by a general director from Russian oil company LUKoil and would be made up of people from the other parties involved.
"We need people with knowledge of the countries involved and we need people with knowledge of the technology we'll be using in order to ensure the best possible product," he said.

CPC includes Chevron with 15 percent, Russia's LUKoil with 12.5 percent, Mobil Corp and Russia's Rosneft with a 7.5 percent stake each, British Gas plc and Italy's Agip with two percent each and Amoco Corp and Oryx Energy with 1.75 percent each. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
